newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Prices mixed at Colombo tea auction.
newsitem.headline: Prices mixed at Colombo tea auction.

text.p: Tea prices at the Colombo auction were varied as brokers and buyers trickled in after holidays.
A smaller than average 3.8 million kilograms were on offer at the year's first auction, which was reduced to one day from the usual two, brokers said.
High growns fell across the board with the best BOPs on offer losing 6-8 rupees per kg, brokers Forbes & Walker said.
Low growns, which had good demand from the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, sold at fully firm to dearer rates, they added.
Iraq was still not back in the Colombo auction because prices were too high, a broker for Forbes said.
"Iraq has been buying from other countries in the region since their prices are lower than ours," he said.
The anticipated gross sale average fell to 101 rupees ($1.78) compared to 102.36 last week, Forbes said.
The next auction is on January 8 with four million kg on offer. ($ = 56.69 rupees)
